title: Branches and loops
summary: Truthiness, if and elseif, the ternary, match, and the three loop forms.

blocks.html:
if accepts any value and asks whether it is true. Most values are, so the rule is easier from the other side — these are falsy: 0, 0.0, "", the string "0", the empty array [], null, and an unset variable.

Everything else is truthy, including " ", "false" and -1. Booleans are required nowhere and allowed everywhere.

blocks.title: truthy and falsy
blocks.code:
<?php

if (0 || "" || "0" || [] || null) {
    echo "at least one was true\n";
} else {
    echo "all of them are falsy\n";
}

if (" " || "0.0" || -1) {
    echo "these are truthy\n";
}
blocks.output:
all of them are falsy
these are truthy

blocks.title: if, elseif, else
blocks.code:
<?php

$finalGrade = 84;

if ($finalGrade >= 90) {
    $remark = "Excellent";
} elseif ($finalGrade >= 80) {
    $remark = "Good";
} elseif ($finalGrade >= 70) {
    $remark = "Fair";
} else {
    $remark = "Failed";
}

echo "84 is ", $remark, "\n";

blocks.html: The string "0" is falsy, so a form field where the visitor typed 0 reads as no answer and if ($submitted) takes the empty branch. When the value came from someone else, compare explicitly: $submitted !== "" is true for "0".

The ternary is an if that produces a value: $cond ? $whenTrue : $whenFalse. Its cousin ?? is the isset question as an expression — take the left side if it exists and is not null, otherwise the right side.

blocks.title: ternary and null coalescing
blocks.output:
Score 74: failed
Retake: yes
Nickname: none set

blocks.html: match is a switch that returns a value. Each arm is a value to compare against and an expression to hand back. The comparison is strict, so "1" and 1 are different arms, and nothing falls through. If no arm matches and there is no default, PHP throws an UnhandledMatchError.

blocks.title: match over the days of the week
match is strict: "1" and 1 are different arms
blocks.code:
<?php

foreach (["1", 1, 8] as $value) {
    echo gettype($value), " => ", match ($value) {
        "1" => "string one",
        1 => "integer one",
        default => "no arm matched",
    }, "\n";
}
blocks.output:
string => string one
integer => integer one
integer => no arm matched

blocks.title: while and for
blocks.code:
<?php

$balance = 5000;
$withdrawn = 0;

// while: keep going while the condition holds
while ($balance >= 1000) {
    $balance -= 1000;
    $withdrawn += 1000;
}

echo "withdrew $withdrawn, left $balance\n";

$total = 0;

// for: counted loop, the counter lives in the head
for ($i = 1; $i <= 5; $i++) {
    $total += $i;
}

echo "1 + 2 + 3 + 4 + 5 = $total\n";

blocks.title: foreach, with break and continue
blocks.code:
<?php

$students = ["Juan", "Maria", "Pedro"];

// foreach: once per element, in order
foreach ($students as $index => $name) {
    echo $index + 1, ". ", $name, "\n";
}

foreach ([3, 7, 12, 15] as $number) {
    if ($number % 2 === 0) {
        continue;      // skip the rest of this turn
    }
    if ($number > 10) {
        break;         // leave the loop completely
    }
    echo $number, "\n";
}

blocks.html:
Those are the three loop forms: while when you do not know how many turns it takes, for when you do, and foreach when you are walking a list. Every one of them can be left early with break or cut short with continue.

Now open public/example.php in the project. The commented-out getDayName() at the top is exactly the match you just ran, wrapped in a function and called from a for loop — the file has been using match all along. Chapter 06 adds the wrapper.

quiz.why: Any non-empty string except the single character 0 is truthy, so "false" passes an if. The string "0" and the empty array are falsy.

quiz.q: What does match return when no arm matches and there is no default?
quiz.why: match has no fallback of its own. Without a default arm an unmatched value is a runtime error, which is why the day example ends with one.

quiz.q: match compares strictly. What happens when 0.1 + 0.2 is matched against the arm 0.3?
options: It matches, because both are floats
It does not match: the sum is not exactly 0.3
quiz.why: match uses ===, and 0.1 + 0.2 stores as 0.30000000000000004, so the arm is skipped and the value falls to default. Round before matching.

exercise.brief: Print one line per day from 1 to 7, in the form 1 => Monday up to 7 => Sunday. Use a for loop and match, with a default arm that reads Invalid input.
exercise.hint: Build the line with echo $day, " => ", match ($day) { ... }, "\n"; — the match arms hold the day names.
